The game behind the journey

Design field notes

The player promise

A cooperative, immersive and relaxing VR game about coexistence in a prehistoric world. Choose your own real dinosaur species before starting as a youngster. Begin alone, discover a hidden haven, make friends, hunt or gather according to your species, and build a family and community.

Eat / Build / Find

Eat: gather plants, hunt wildlife, or fish as diet allows. Build: push rocks, drag branches, gather straw, form nests, make fallen-tree crossings, and trample paths. Find: discover land, animals, other dinosaurs, a home, a partner, and lost hatchlings. Each activity should lead to a mission, a destination, a decision, and visible feedback.

Community and family

Both human players and AI inhabit the community. Members cannot hunt each other. Players can keep their own family or join a shared household. Switch between family members; AI keeps the previous dinosaur near home and handles basic needs. Family formation follows maturity.

Growth and inherited traits

Activities develop abilities during a lifetime. Parents' activities and the offspring's habitat unlock traits that players choose to develop across generations. These are fictional gameplay adaptations. This short demo records possible trait directions; it does not simulate generations.

Danger, protection, and time away

Gentle exploration includes serious risks. Permanent family or egg loss is possible during active play, with clear warnings and rescue opportunities. Family needs pause while household players are offline. This demonstration ends each mission safely and illustrates the warning-and-response flow without simulating permanent loss.

VR embodiment and prototype boundaries

The intended VR controls use the headset for looking and controllers for forelimbs. Species-specific reach, movement comfort, and natural construction need headset testing. This HTML experience is a clickable design document, not a VR build. Nestbound is a working title; the three species, cast, missions, trait names, and numerical outcomes shown here are proposals. Final roster, headset, player count, and multiplayer architecture remain open.
